001package com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog;
002
003import org.apache.commons.lang3.Validate;
004import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.annotations.HistoryLogProps;
005import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.helpers.Bytes;
006
007/**
008 * A press or release of the pump's button, with a millisecond timestamp. Seen on the t:slim X2 and
009 * the Tandem Mobi.
010 *
011 * <p>Tandem's export and its Mobi app do not name this opcode, so the class name and the button
012 * interpretation are provisional. The layout is well supported: uint32 {@code timeOfDayMs} at
013 * bytes 10-13, {@code state} at byte 14, zeros at 15-25 (1772/1772 records from at least 8 pumps,
014 * X2 and Mobi).
015 *
016 * <p>The button reading rests on three observations. On the Mobi, where tubing is filled by holding
017 * the pump button, every tubing-prime start ({@link PrimeInprocessHistoryLog}) was immediately
018 * preceded by one of these with state 1 (113/113 on 4 pumps). A triple press (1, 0, 1, 0, 1 within
019 * 0.6 s) was immediately followed by a {@link SnoozeActivatedHistoryLog} in the same second. On the
020 * X2, whose button wakes the screen, press/release pairs typically last about 0.2 s.
021 * See https://github.com/jwoglom/pumpx2/issues/148.
022 */
023@HistoryLogProps(
024    opCode = 17,
025    displayName = "Pump Button",
026    internalName = ""
027)
028public class PumpButtonHistoryLog extends HistoryLog {
029
030    private long timeOfDayMs;
031    private int state;
032
033    public PumpButtonHistoryLog() {}
034    public PumpButtonHistoryLog(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, long timeOfDayMs, int state) {
035        super(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum);
036        this.cargo = buildCargo(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum, timeOfDayMs, state);
037        this.timeOfDayMs = timeOfDayMs;
038        this.state = state;
039    }
040
041    public int typeId() {
042        return 17;
043    }
044
045    /**
046     * <table border="1">
047     * <caption>Parsed fields for PumpButtonHistoryLog:</caption>
048     * <tr><td><code>timeOfDayMs</code></td><td><code>Bytes.readUint32(raw, 10)</code></td></tr>
049     * <tr><td><code>state</code></td><td><code>raw[14] &amp; 0xFF</code></td></tr>
050     * </table>
051     */
052    public void parse(byte[] raw) {
053        Validate.isTrue(raw.length == 26);
054        this.cargo = raw;
055        parseBase(raw);
056        this.timeOfDayMs = Bytes.readUint32(raw, 10);
057        this.state = raw[14] & 0xFF;
058    }
059
060    public static byte[] buildCargo(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, long timeOfDayMs, int state) {
061        return HistoryLog.fillCargo(Bytes.combine(
062            HistoryLog.typeIdBytes(17, 0),
063            Bytes.toUint32(pumpTimeSec),
064            Bytes.toUint32(sequenceNum),
065            Bytes.toUint32(timeOfDayMs),
066            new byte[]{ (byte) state }));
067    }
068
069    /**
070     * Milliseconds since midnight on the pump's local clock, the same clock as
071     * {@link #getPumpTimeSec()}: {@code timeOfDayMs / 1000 == pumpTimeSec % 86400} in 1772/1772
072     * records. It gives sub-second ordering within the record's second; it is not a motor or
073     * encoder count.
074     */
075    public long getTimeOfDayMs() {
076        return timeOfDayMs;
077    }
078
079    /**
080     * Byte 14: 1 or 0, alternating (880 records with 1, 892 with 0). Read as 1 = pressed,
081     * 0 = released; see the class comment for why that reading is provisional.
082     */
083    public int getState() {
084        return state;
085    }
086
087    public boolean isPressed() {
088        return state == 1;
089    }
090}
